title: Critical Zscaler Client Connector Vulnerability Allows Remote Code Execution Without Login
content_md: A critical vulnerability in its Client Connector endpoint application that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code without requiring user interaction or valid login credentials. Tracked as CVE-2026-59568, the flaw has received a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.1 and is classified as Critical. The vulnerability is remotely exploitable over a network and requires neither privileges nor user interaction, creating a potentially severe exposure for enterprises that use Zscaler Client Connector on managed Windows endpoints . The vulnerability carries the CVSS vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N , indicating that exploitation requires low attack complexity and can be initiated through network access. Critical Zscaler Client Connector Vulnerability A successful attack could enable high-impact compromise of confidentiality and integrity, although the advisory does not identify an availability impact. Zscaler’s 2026 Client Connector release summary indicates that CVE-2026-59568 addresses multiple remote code execution vulnerabilities rather than a single isolated flaw. This lack of public exploit information means defenders currently have limited options for developing reliable network-based detection signatures or indicators of compromise. Zscaler included fixes for the RCE vulnerabilities in Client Connector releases published on June 1, 2026. For Windows systems, version 4.8.0.232 is identified as mitigating the multiple RCE issues associated with CVE-2026-5956
